title: Autoresearch Made Our Models 3x Faster — Tejas Bhakta, Morph
talk_summary: Tejas Bhakta describes 'autoresearch' — a while-loop where an agent proposes a change, a verifiable benchmark scores it, and the change is kept or reverted — applied to GPU kernel optimization. The key lessons are that verifiable goals plus explicit 'what not to do' constraints prevent reward hacking, and that ~80% of agent proposals are bad but the loop still yields 3x speedups.

takeaways.technique: Keep-or-revert loop against a verifiable benchmark
takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap agent proposals in a while loop: propose a change, run a correctness+speed benchmark, keep if it improves, revert otherwise, repeat until goal met.
takeaways.numbers: 3x speedup end-to-end; ~80% of proposals are bad

takeaways.technique: Explicit anti-goals / 'what not to do' constraints
takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent a written list of forbidden shortcuts (e.g. don't disable CUDA graphs, don't only test small contexts) because agents optimize the metric by cheating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of this is also just defining what not to do which is actually very important

takeaways.what_they_do: Feed the agent markdown files describing the exact hardware features and model architecture, because without them it hallucinates the mechanism and produces useless output.

takeaways.technique: Route by task fit, not by brand
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes some models (notably Anthropic ones) fail to emit the required DSL, and recommends switching models rather than fighting it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some models just don't actually write the cute DSL you need ... I would recommend using a different model

takeaways.technique: Human sets direction, agent searches parameters
takeaways.what_they_do: Humans supply the high-level idea; the loop only tunes parameters and verifies. Agents are explicitly bad at the 'groundbreaking idea'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it is still your job to have good ideas ... auto research picks out the parameters

takeaways.technique: Benchmark must cover the full end-to-end path
takeaways.what_they_do: Warns that optimizing one kernel while disabling a global speedup makes the whole system slower — the metric must be end-to-end, not local.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they might make that one kernel faster but make the whole ... it's not a viable kernel
takeaways.numbers: disabling CUDA graphs can be 20x slower
